subsystems.name: Cell source and bioink
subsystems.role: provides the living cells and the printable matrix that carries them.
parts: induced pluripotent stem cells or primary cells

subsystems.name: Bioprinter
subsystems.role: deposits bioink in precise three-dimensional patterns.

subsystems.name: Tissue scaffold
subsystems.role: mimics the organ's architecture and extracellular matrix.

subsystems.name: Microfluidic chip
subsystems.role: supplies nutrients and removes waste, mimicking blood flow.

subsystems.name: Sensing and imaging
subsystems.role: measures how the tissue responds to drugs or disease.

subsystems.name: Environmental control
subsystems.role: keeps the living tissue stable and alive.
parts: gas mixer for oxygen and carbon dioxide

buildSteps.title: Obtain and expand cells
buildSteps.detail: Stem cells are grown and chemically guided to become the organ-specific cell types needed, such as liver or heart cells.

buildSteps.title: Formulate bioink
buildSteps.detail: Cells are mixed with a hydrogel and growth factors to a consistency that can be printed without clogging or killing the cells.

buildSteps.title: Design the organ model
buildSteps.detail: Software creates a three-dimensional blueprint of the organ's microarchitecture, including channels for nutrients.

buildSteps.title: Print the tissue
buildSteps.detail: The bioprinter deposits bioink layer by layer, building up a living construct that matches the blueprint.

buildSteps.title: Mature the tissue
buildSteps.detail: The printed construct is incubated so cells can attach, multiply and self-organise into functional tissue.

buildSteps.title: Integrate onto chip
buildSteps.detail: The matured tissue is placed inside a microfluidic chip, and tubing connects it to a perfusion system.

buildSteps.title: Perfuse and stabilise
buildSteps.detail: Culture medium is pumped through the chip to deliver oxygen and nutrients and carry away waste, mimicking blood flow.

buildSteps.title: Dose and test
buildSteps.detail: Candidate drugs are introduced at different concentrations, and the tissue's response is monitored over hours or days.

buildSteps.title: Analyse response
buildSteps.detail: Sensors and imaging record changes in cell viability, metabolism or gene activity, which are compared with known human or animal data.

prerequisites.why: provides a renewable source of human cells that can become many organ types.
can place cells in 3D, but fine resolution and thick-tissue vascularisation remain difficult.
creates the organ-on-chip environment that keeps small tissues alive and supplies flow.
hydrogels must mimic the extracellular matrix closely enough for cells to behave as they do in the body.
some regulators now consider non-animal methods, but full replacement of animal trials for most drugs is not yet approved.

pathway.milestone: organ-on-chip models used for toxicity screening in some drug development programmes
pathway.unlocks: early filtering of unsafe compounds without animals, but only alongside traditional tests.

pathway.milestone: multi-organ chips that link several printed tissues, such as liver and heart, on one platform
pathway.unlocks: better prediction of how a drug affects the whole body, including organ interactions.

pathway.milestone: patient-derived cells used to build personalised organ models
pathway.unlocks: testing drugs on a specific person's cells before treatment.

pathway.milestone: validated bioprinted organoids-on-chip accepted as a primary safety and efficacy test for certain drug classes
pathway.unlocks: a substantial reduction, and in some cases replacement, of animal trials.
